steps: Choose the design option

Standard, Komfort Zone Kit (#KZK-062), heat transfer kits (HTK-INT / HTK-EXT, up to 2) or Kozy Power Vent (#KPV, horizontal only). Framing, clearances and venting depend on it; standard and KZK need an 80" minimum chamber and ceiling height.

Decide before setting the unit: framing, clearance to combustibles and vent configuration all depend on it.

  • Standard: follow the sections marked 'standard installation'. Fireplace chamber and ceiling at least 80" (2032mm).
  • Komfort Zone Kit (#KZK-062): redistributes radiant heat through a plenum, allowing combustible facing above, heat reduction for a TV and lower mantel clearances. Framing and clearances may differ: use the KZK manual. 80" (2032mm) minimum height.
  • Heat transfer kits (HTK-INT / HTK-EXT): up to (2) at once, same or mixed. With a standard install the minimums in this manual apply; cover plates come off (section 4.2).
  • Kozy Power Vent (#KPV): fan-powered mechanical draft, horizontal terminations only, with either option. It doesn't change facing, finishing or safety barrier requirements.

The manual also allows a bedroom installation; an aftermarket, permanently located manufactured home (USA only) or mobile home where local codes don't prohibit it (p. 1); and an outdoor covered area protected from direct precipitation, approved for operation from 40°F to 110°F (section 3.10). If you plan to convert to propane, it's easier before the unit goes into the framed opening.
Frame the opening

Rough-in per Figure 3.5 (the same for every design option) on nominal 2" x 4" framing; lay out the vent path first. Set the unit on a level wood or non-combustible surface; the fireplace isn't load-bearing.

The rough-in dimensions are given only in Figure 3.5, a diagram on this page; take them from the drawing. All clearances and images assume nominal 2" x 4" framing.

  • Lay out the vent run before installing the appliance. If possible, place the unit so the vent terminates between two studs.
  • Level surface able to support the fireplace and venting. All framing, facing and finishing material must be self-supported.
  • Bottom directly on wood or a non-combustible surface (not linoleum or carpet). On carpeting, tile or other combustible material other than wood flooring, use a metal or wood panel the full width and depth. Above floor level: a solid, continuous platform.
  • Floor protection in front of the fireplace is not required.
  • Cold air transfer area: insulate outside walls. Masonry above: a foundation for the full load and a lintel over the appliance.
  • TV above: the KZK option is highly recommended. Allowed TV recess 4-1/4" (108mm), front of the 2x4 framing to the back of the pocket's finishing material.
  • Wall thimble rough-in: Figure 3.8 (p. 21), based on Simpson DuraVent pipe.
KZK / HTK prep (if used)

KZK-062: remove the 2 top cover plates (16 screws), fit the KZK collars, remove and discard the 2 convection baffles. HTK: remove the side cover plate and lifting handle and fit the HTK-NTL air chute; the damper stays for HTK-EXT and comes out for HTK-INT.

Sections 3.4 and 3.5 say to complete this preparation before setting the appliance in the framed opening and before assembling the top stand-offs.

Komfort Zone Kit (KZK-062)

  1. Remove the (16) sheet metal screws holding the (2) cover plates at the top of the fireplace. Discard the plates; keep the screws.
  2. Install the KZK collars supplied with KZK-062, reusing those screws.
  3. Remove the (2) convection baffles ((2) screws each) and discard baffles and screws.

Heat transfer kit (HTK-INT / HTK-EXT)

  1. Remove the HTK cover plate on that side; keep its (4) sheet metal screws.
  2. Remove the lifting handle; keep its (9) screws.
  3. Install the HTK-NTL air chute with the saved screws and those supplied with it, then attach its collar.
  4. HTK-EXT: the damper stays, resting flat and free to move. HTK-INT: remove the damper.
Note: p. 13 says the Section 4.0 preparation must be completed before setting the appliance in the framed opening; the HTK instructions on p. 26 recommend installing the fireplace in the framed opening before removing the lifting handle.
Stand-offs, flanges & set the unit

Attach the top stand-off brackets (4 screws) and heat shields (8 screws) before positioning; they give the 7-7/8" header clearance. Fit the nailing flanges (3-1/4" side clearance), team-lift the unit in and secure it flush with the framing.

Screws are in the fireplace components packet.

Top stand-off assembly (before positioning)

  1. Attach the top stand-off brackets to the top of the fireplace with (4) screws.
  2. Bend the screw-hole tabs on the horizontal heat shields upward and attach the shields to the brackets with (8) screws.

The top stand-offs provide the 7-7/8" (200mm) minimum clearance to the header. Use only non-combustible material in that zone, the full width of the fireplace: no wood or sheetrock.

Nailing flanges

  1. Remove the (2) nailing flanges from the sides and align them with the holes on the outside corners, stand-off flanges facing away from the fireplace.
  2. Screw them on through the slots, then bend the perforation until parallel with the fireplace face (never toward it).
  3. Set the framing stud against the small stand-off on the back of the flange and nail or screw it.

The flanges give the 3-1/4" (83mm) minimum side clearance to framing. Never permanently remove these assemblies.

Set the unit

It's heavy: team lift, by hand on the side lift handles or with a 2" x 4" through them. Place it in the framed opening and secure it; it sits flush with the framing.
Vent system

5" x 8" co-axial pipe from an approved maker. Fit the restrictor plate before attaching the vent, and install the vent heat shield in every scenario; 1/4" rise per 12" of horizontal travel. Never connect to a flue serving a solid-fuel appliance.

• 5" (127mm) exhaust x 8" (203mm) intake co-axial pipe from an approved manufacturer, or reduced 4" x 6-5/8" for vertical terminations; run limits under the Venting spec.
  • Restrictor plate (components packet): ships with both inner rings intact, the most restriction. Install it per Figure 7.3 before attaching the venting.
  • Vent heat shields: front vertical shield when the pipe terminates at the enclosure ceiling; front vertical plus top horizontal shield at the minimum wall run.
  • Horizontal sections: 1/4" (6mm) rise per 12" (305mm). Wall thimbles that meet the 1" (25mm) top clearance for every wall the run passes through. Don't recess the cap into the wall or siding.
  • Flexible vent pipe only outside the appliance enclosure, and never to terminate.
  • Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.
  • Never connect to a chimney flue serving a separate solid-fuel appliance.
Gas line + leak test

Listed ½" tee-handle shut-off and flexible connector to the ½" valve inlet (licensed plumber or gas fitter in Massachusetts). Disconnect for system tests above ½ psi; check every connection with soapy water.

• Manufactured for natural gas. If converting to propane, do it first (see Fuel & conversion).
  • Gas line by a qualified person to local codes, or the National Fuel Gas Code ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54 or CSA B149.1. Massachusetts: licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • A listed (Massachusetts-approved) ½" (13mm) tee-handle manual shut-off valve and flexible gas connector connect to the ½" (13mm) control valve inlet. The fireplace comes with a 3/8" (10mm) x 18" (457mm) flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve.
  • Bring the line in through the gas line hole (Figure 2.2) and don't route it where it would obstruct the fan.
  • System pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At ½ psi or less: close its manual shut-off valve.
  • Check all connections for leaks with soapy water, whether field or factory made.
Electrical
120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps to the junction box. The supply must be hot at all times with no switch in it; ground per local codes or ANSI/NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1.

• Junction box: 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps. Shut off the household breaker before working on any electrical lines.
  • The AC power supply must be hot at all times and must not have a switch installed in it.
  • Three-prong grounding plug into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle; never cut or remove the grounding prong.
  • Ground per local codes, or the National Electrical Code ANSI/NFPA 70 or the Canadian Electrical Code CSA C22.1.
  • Outdoor covered installs: all wiring to the outdoor requirements of NFPA 70.
  • Wiring diagrams: Figures 9.1–9.3, pp. 56–58.
Finishing

Non-combustible facing only in the zones of Figure 5.6 (ASTM E 136; drywall, including Type X, and WonderBoard don't qualify). Keep mantels, surround and hearth within section 5.1; finishes must not block ventilation air.

• Non-combustible facing and finishing only where Figure 5.6 (p. 34, a diagram) shows it; the same figure marks where screws aren't allowed. Material must meet ASTM E 136. Paper-faced gypsum board (including Type X) and WonderBoard aren't non-combustible.
  • Combustible mantel: a 6" (152mm) mantel starts 12" (305mm) above the top finishing edge; depth can increase 1" (25mm) per 1" (25mm) of height.
  • Non-combustible mantel: up to 8" (203mm) deep at 0" from the top finishing edge, then 1" up for every 1" deeper. Non-combustible surround: up to 8" (203mm) projection at 0" from the side and top finishing edges.
  • Combustible hearth: unlimited projection, at 0" (flush) to the bottom finishing edge. Combustible sidewall: unlimited, at 0" from the side finishing edge; allow 3/4" (19mm) with the NK60TL-RS rectangle surround.
  • Finishing material can't obstruct ventilation air. Never use one U-shaped piece of marble, granite or stone around the opening; stone must handle temperatures greater than 160°F.
  • To reduce cracking above: dry, dust-free surfaces; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound such as Durabond; high-quality acrylic latex primer and finish; avoid flat or light-colored paints.
  • A Komfort Zone Kit changes these requirements: follow its manual.
Bulbs, panels, logs & screen
Convert to propane first if needed. Fit the 7 front ember-bed halogen bulbs (not factory-installed), then the panel set, then the NK60TL-500 or NK60TL-B501 log set, then the safety screen barrier.

1. If converting to propane, do it before installing any light kit components, panel set or log set.
  2. Front bottom light kit (power off): remove the (2) screws and lift out the front ember media tray, fit the (7) halogen bulbs from the components packet, reinstall the tray. Never touch the bulbs with bare hands; use a soft cloth.
  3. The back bottom and top light kits have their halogen bulbs installed at the factory.
  4. Optional panel set per its own instructions, before the logs. Then the log set: Traditional NK60TL-500 or Birch NK60TL-B501, per its instructions.
  5. Safety screen barrier: hook its two mounting hooks per side into the slots between the glass frame and the side finishing edge, lift and push toward the fireplace. It's seated when the spacing is even on all four sides.
  6. Optional NK60TL-RS rectangle surround: (4) truss head screws to the (2) mounting nuts on each side; it takes up to 1-5/8" (41mm) of facing and finishing material.
Initialize & test

Clear packaging from the firebox, sync the remote (3 beeps, ON/OFF within 5 seconds, 4 beeps), then check inlet and manifold pressure at the IN/OUT taps. Burn 15 minutes before any venturi or restrictor-plate adjustment.

1. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF, put (3) AAA batteries in the remote and connect the IFC module to AC power.
  2. Remove the safety screen and component access cover. Press the remote sync button: the IFC module beeps (3) times and lights an amber LED.
  3. Within (5) seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: (4) beeps, and the pilot lights (the igniter sparks repeatedly; the pilot ignites if gas is supplied).
  4. Press ON/OFF again; the pilot goes out and the system is initialized. Set the rocker switch to ON and reinstall the covers.
  5. Inlet pressure at the IN tap with all other gas appliances on, then manifold pressure at the OUT tap at low and high (see the pressure specs). After each reading: turn off burner and pilot, disconnect the hose and tighten the tap clockwise (snug, don't over-tighten), relight pilot and burner, then re-attach the manometer to verify the tap is completely sealed: it should read no pressure.
  6. Flames start blue and gradually turn yellow during the first 15 minutes. If they stay blue or turn dark orange with soot, a qualified service technician adjusts the venturis in slight increments.
  7. Vertical terminations may show an active, compact flame: install or modify the restrictor plate (tabs bent to approximately 80°, into the 5" (127mm) exhaust, tabs toward you). Burn at least 15 minutes and let it cool between adjustments.

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power, or use battery backup with fully charged batteries
Wiring disconnected → check every connection against the wiring schematic (section 9.0)
Gas supply off → check the shut-offs; there may be more than one valve between appliance and main line
No propane, or low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → refill; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten
Pilot not contacting the flame rectification sensor → verify it envelops the top of the sensor and reaches the burner

panels.title: Main burner won't light
items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → switch it ON
Gas supply off or low → check for multiple shut-offs and the propane tank; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Wiring disconnected or wrong → check against section 9.0
Plugged burner orifice → remove the blockage
Pilot flame not directed to ignite the burner → see the pilot causes
Remote not working → replace batteries · no call for heat → remote ON, thermostat operation OFF

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: No propane in tank → refill
Firebox glass assembly installed incorrectly → see section 8.1
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Horizontal vent without 1/4" (6mm) rise per 12" (305mm) of travel
Exhaust leaking back into the firebox → check for leaks and repair
Excessive draft → install or modify the restrictor plate (11.2.3)

panels.title: Soot on glass · blue, lifting flame
items: Soot: log or burner/perimeter media out of place → reposition per the instructions
Soot: venturi setting → open the air shutter slightly (more air)
Blue flame lifting off the burner: venturi setting → close the air shutter slightly (less air)
Either: vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked; for a lifting flame also check the vent pipes for leaks

codes: Backup pack under 4V; low double-beep on ON/OFF. Replace the batteries.
No flame after 2 ignition tries. Verify gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset (10.7.1) or re-initialize (10.2).

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
This fireplace lights itself: an igniter lights the pilot automatically. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Everyday on and off

  1. Press ON/OFF on the remote. One beep confirms, and about 4 seconds later the control starts sparking at the pilot.
  2. Press ON/OFF again to turn it off. One beep, and the main burner shuts off.

The ON/OFF rocker switch behind the component access cover must be set to ON for the remote to run the fireplace.

The full lighting procedure (from the label)

  1. Press OFF on the remote and turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  2. Find the manual gas valve your service technician installed and turn it clockwise to OFF. Use your hand only, never tools.
  3. Wait 5 minutes, then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow "Safety & gas smell."
  4. No gas smell: turn the valve counterclockwise to ON, turn the power back on and press ON on the remote.
Won't start? Turn the gas off (remote OFF, then the manual valve clockwise to OFF) and call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote takes (3) AAA batteries in the bay at its base. Most commands are confirmed by a single beep from the fireplace.

ON/OFFturns the fireplace on or off
Up / Downflame height, 6 levels; Down to OFF, then Up relights on HI
Thermostat keyroom thermostat, or SMART
Mode keysteps to the fan, light and AUX icons

Thermostat

Press the thermostat key to see the room and set temperatures, then use the arrows to pick a temperature. Press it until "SMART" appears and the flame turns down by itself when the room reaches your set point. While SMART is on, you can't adjust the flame by hand.

Fan and lights

  • Fan (optional kit): Mode to the fan icon, then the arrows for off, on and 6 speeds. In thermostat mode it waits 5 minutes after lighting and runs about 12 minutes after shut-off.
  • Top light: Mode to the light icon; 6 brightness levels.
  • Ember bed light: Mode to AUX; Up for on, Down for off. The manual first has you activate AUX in the remote's setup. Its brightness knob is under the firebox, behind the component access cover.

Key lock: press Mode and Up together. °F or °C: with the fireplace off, press thermostat and Mode together.

sounds.title: Beeps, sparks and other normal things
sounds.html:
Beeps

  • One beep: your remote command was received.
  • A low double-beep when you press ON/OFF: the backup batteries are low. It won't take commands until they're replaced.
  • Three beeps and an amber light, then four beeps: the remote is being paired with the fireplace.

Sparking at start-up

About 4 seconds after you press ON, the igniter sparks at the pilot. If the pilot doesn't light, it sparks for up to 60 seconds, pauses about 35 seconds, then tries once more.

A short pause once a day

When the pilot has stayed lit, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours to run a safety check, then goes back to your last command.

Flame and noises

When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue and gradually turn yellow during the first 15 minutes. Some minor expansion, contraction or movement of parts that makes noise is normal and not a defect. Finishing materials around the fireplace can off-gas or smell when heated; Kozy Heat doesn't guarantee those materials.

Flames that stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips and soot, need a qualified service technician to adjust.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is your job once a year. Never remove or clean it while it's hot; wait until the fireplace has fully cooled.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Lift off the safety screen.
  3. Using the glass latch tool from the components packet, pull the 4 spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox out and up.
  4. Tilt the top of the glass toward you and lift it off the support rail at the bottom.
  5. Clean it with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. No abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  6. Put the glass back in reverse order, then the safety screen. Don't run the fireplace without the screen.
Cracked or broken? Don't use the fireplace, and wear gloves to handle broken glass. The glass and its latches are the pressure-relief system; Hussong supplies replacement glass only as a complete assembly, fitted by a qualified service person. Avoid striking or slamming it.
Note: p. 46 describes 4 spring-loaded latches holding the glass at the top of the firebox; the yearly service list on p. 72 refers to a bottom latch assembly.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
modes.html:
Your fireplace can run its pilot two ways, and you choose with the remote.

IPI (on-demand pilot)no snowflake on the remote screen while it's on
CPI (continuous pilot)snowflake icon on the remote screen while it's on

IPI sparks the pilot alight when it's needed. CPI keeps a standing pilot lit, which keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the main burner lights with less air-flow disruption.

Switching modes

  1. With the fireplace off, press Mode until the CPI icon is selected.
  2. Press Up for CPI, or Down to go back to IPI. A single beep confirms.

The 7-day timer

In CPI, if the main burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off. That's a standard safety feature of the SIT Proflame 2 system. Each time the burner lights, the timer starts over at 7 days.

Pilot always on and won't go out? The control is set to CPI. Switch it to IPI.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on 120 VAC house power and/or batteries. Its power supply must stay on at all times; there's no switch in it.

During an outage

  • The burner and flame height adjustment keep working on the backup battery pack.
  • The fan and the lights don't work until the power comes back.
  • How long the backup batteries last depends on their quality, how many times it lights and other factors.

Low-battery signs

Backup pack lowlow double-beep when you press ON/OFF; red light blinks once, in intervals
Remote lowbattery icon on the remote screen

When the backup pack is low, the fireplace won't accept commands until you replace its batteries; it beeps once as soon as it has power again. The remote takes (3) AAA batteries, and its battery icon disappears once they're replaced.

trouble.title: If it won't light or respond
trouble.html:
When you press ON, the control makes two tries at lighting the pilot. If neither works, it locks out and the red light on the control module (behind the component access cover) blinks 3 times, over and over, until it's reset.

Reset after a lockout

  1. Press ON/OFF on the remote to turn the system off.
  2. Wait about 2 seconds and press ON/OFF again. The lighting sequence starts over.

What the red light means

1 blinkbackup batteries low: replace them
2 blinkspilot flame error: contact your dealer
3 blinkslockout: make sure the gas is on, then reset

Quick checks

  • Remote does nothing: replace the remote or backup batteries. It may also need re-pairing to the fireplace, or a reset after too many failed tries.
  • Burner won't come on: the rocker switch is ON, the gas supply is on (there may be more than one shut-off), the propane tank isn't empty, and thermostat operation is off on the remote.
  • Pilot won't go out: it's set to CPI. Switch to IPI.
Beyond these basics, the manual says troubleshooting must be done by a qualified technician.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building immediately.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before you light the fireplace, smell around it, including next to the floor: some gas is heavier than air and settles there.

Hot glass and children

Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. The safety screen supplied with the fireplace must stay on; if it's damaged, replace it with Hussong's screen for this model. Supervise young children closely in the same room; an adjustable safety gate can keep toddlers out of the room.

Also

  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from the fireplace, and never store or use gasoline or flammable liquids nearby.
  • Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
  • Turn the gas valve by hand only, never with tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it; call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpet, bedding or pets can mean it needs cleaning more often.

What the service person does each year

  • Vacuums the firebox and checks that the glass latches move freely.
  • Disconnects and vacuums the fan, if fitted. Its bearings are sealed and need no oil.
  • Inspects the vent and vent cap for soot or blockage.
  • Cleans the glass and inspects it for cracks, scratches and nicks.
  • Vacuums the burner, checks gas connections for leaks, and checks the pilot, the burner flame and the safety shut-off timing.

Your part

  • Clean the glass once a year (see "Clean the glass").
  • Keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that can burn, and of gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.
  • Top light bulbs are replaced as needed by a qualified service person.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg.'s limited lifetime warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship, from the date of purchase, for the original purchaser only.

30 days, parts & laborpaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1, parts & laborall other parts and material
Years 2 to lifetime, parts onlyfirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model; nothing needs to be sent in to register. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids it or isn't covered

  • Installation by anyone other than a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not following the manual
  • A removed serial number or testing label, or an altered fireplace
  • Submersion in water or long periods of dampness
  • Normal wear and tear, venting or environmental problems, and non-Hussong parts such as chimney components
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

specInput.title: Input rates
specInput.html:
NG max / min51,000 / 34,000 Btu/h (14.95 / 9.96 kW)
LP max / min51,000 / 40,000 Btu/h (14.95 / 11.72 kW)

High altitude

US: above 2,000' (610m), reduce input ratings 4% for each 1,000' (305m) above sea level. Canada: above 4,500' (1,372m), reduce the certified high-altitude rating 4% for each additional 1,000' (305m). The manual lists CSA 2.17 2017 (Gas-Fired Appliances for Use at High Altitudes) among its standards.

Burners are referenced as left, center, right and bottom (Figure 2.1, p. 9). Orifice and venturi settings by fuel are under Fuel & conversion.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
NG minimum5" WC (1.25 kPa)
NG recommended7" WC (1.74 kPa)
NG maximum10" WC (2.49 kPa)
LP minimum12" WC (2.99 kPa) or 11" WC (2.74 kPa)
LP maximum13" WC (3.24 kPa)
Note: the specifications table on p. 8 gives a propane minimum inlet pressure of 12" WC (2.99 kPa); Table 6.1 on p. 35 gives 11" WC (2.74 kPa).

Test at the valve's IN tap with a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose, pilot and burner lit, and all other gas appliances in the house on at full capacity. Too high or too low: contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician adjusts incoming pressure (p. 68). Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve for system pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); at ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.

After the reading: turn off burner and pilot, disconnect the manometer hose and tighten the IN tap by turning the screw clockwise (snug, don't over-tighten). Relight pilot and burner, then re-attach the manometer to the IN tap to verify it is completely sealed: it should read no pressure.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
NG high / low3.5" / 1.6" WC (0.87 / 0.40 kPa)
LP high / low10" / 6.4" WC (2.49 / 1.59 kPa)

Test at the valve's OUT tap: light the pilot, loosen the tap screw counter-clockwise, attach a manometer with a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose, light the burner and read it at the low and high settings. Turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the manometer hose and tighten the OUT tap by turning the screw clockwise (snug, don't over-tighten). Relight pilot and burner, then re-attach the manometer to the tap to verify it is completely sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on (p. 68).

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Co-axial 5" (127mm) exhaust x 8" (203mm) air intake, natural draft, horizontal or vertical. Approved makers: American Metal Products (Ameri-Vent), BDM, ICC, Metal Fab, Selkirk and Simpson DuraVent; cap part numbers are in Tables 7.2 and 7.3. Kozy Power Vent #KPV (sold separately) per its own manual.

Horizontal (5" x 8")

12" (304mm) vertical24" (610mm) max horizontal
24" (610mm) vertical8' (2.44m) max horizontal
36" (914mm) vertical12' (3.66m) max horizontal
25' (7.62m) max vertical25' (7.62m) max horizontal

Each minimum is the vertical pipe + 90° elbow + cap. Combination runs (5" x 8" only): 25' (7.62m) max rise + 25' (7.62m) max run = 50' (15.2m) total, with the termination inside the shaded area of Figure 7.8 (p. 44, a diagram). Up to (5) 90° elbows, subtracting 3' (914mm) for each after the first; (2) 45° may replace one 90°, subtracting 18" (457mm) each. Horizontal sections: 1/4" (6mm) rise per 12" (305mm).

Reduced 4" x 6-5/8" venting "is only approved for vertical terminations with the exclusion of the #KPV Power Vent Termination" (Table 7.3 lists the KPV).

Class A / masonry chimney conversion

4" aluminum flex inside an existing chimney of at least 7" ID: 4" x 6-5/8" reducer + retro connector + 10' (3.05m) min / 50' (15.24m) max of 4" flex + top adapter + cap, with 0" to 24" (610mm) of horizontal run. Have the chimney inspected first by a qualified chimney sweep or professional installer, and check that local jurisdiction allows it (p. 45).

Never connect to a chimney flue serving a separate solid-fuel appliance. The vent heat shield is required in every venting scenario; fit the restrictor plate before attaching the vent. Flexible vent pipe only outside the appliance enclosure, never to terminate.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Junction box120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps
Supplyhot at all times, no switch installed
Plugthree-prong grounding, into a grounded receptacle
Remote(3) AAA

Shut off the household breaker before working on electrical lines. Ground per local codes, or ANSI/NFPA 70 or CSA C22.1 (p. 56). On battery backup the burner and flame modulation work; fan and lights don't. The optional #SL42-028 fan kit (two fans) plugs into the receptacle on the IFC control module (p. 55). Wiring diagrams: Figures 9.1–9.3 (pp. 56–58).

specFuel.title: Fuel & conversion
specFuel.html:

conflicts.issue: Propane minimum inlet pressure: 12" WC (2.99 kPa) in the specifications table vs 11" WC (2.74 kPa) in Table 6.1.

Conversion kit: the cover says a conversion kit is supplied with the appliance and the panel/log sections refer to conversion instructions included with the fireplace, but 8.3 says the conversion kit is sold separately; section 6 says the stepper motor is sold separately.
Glass latches: 8.1.1 describes (4) spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox; the 12.1 annual firebox service refers to inspecting a bottom latch assembly.

HTK sequence: 3.4 says Section 4.0 (KZK/HTK) preparation must be completed before setting the appliance in the framed opening; 4.2, whose step 2 removes the lifting handle, recommends installing the fireplace in the framed opening before removing the handle.

review.notes: Text gaps: pp. 2, 4, 6 and 82 are blank and p. 5 (contents) has no text. Section headings and many figures/tables exist only as images, so the guide points to their pages instead of transcribing them: Figure 2.2 dimensions (p. 10), Figure 2.3 screen dimensions (p. 11), Figure 3.5 framing (p. 18), Figure 3.8 wall thimble (p. 21), Figure 5.6 non-combustible zone (p. 34), Figures 7.2 and 7.6-7.8 termination and combination-vent zones (pp. 37, 42-44), wiring Figures 9.1-9.3 (pp. 56-58), and Tables 11.1-11.5 plus flame Figures 11.3, 12.2, 12.3 (pp. 68-74). Catalog: BTU (NG 51,000/34,000, LP 51,000/40,000), 5 x 8 venting, optional fan and IPI match the manual. Not in the manual text, so not checked: efficiency (71.94% NG / 74.63% LP AFUE), height/width/depth (46.125 / 69.5 / 19.5 in), weight (355 lb) and view area (60" x 20"; the manual only gives the 61-3/4" x 22-1/8" glass part, p. 79). The catalog has no model number; the manual's is NDK-60-TL. The backup battery pack's battery type and count are never stated, so the guide doesn't name them. Page 43's footer reads 'GEN-6020 - PFS Report No. 24-181' (another model's footer). Quoted rather than resolved: reduced 4" x 6-5/8" venting 'is only approved for vertical terminations with the exclusion of the #KPV Power Vent Termination', while Table 7.3 lists the KPV (p. 40). The lighting label (p. 59) calls it 'an on-demand pilot that shuts off after 7 days'; 10.2 and 10.9.3 tie the 7-day shutoff to CPI, which the guide follows. Top-light bulb access differs (8.3.3, p. 49: screen, access cover, glass; 12.6, p. 74: screen, exterior media tray, glass); the owner side leaves bulbs to a service person. The troubleshooting chart's issue/cause grouping was read from the table layout and the raw text order; 'pilot will not light' and 'will not stay lit' are merged into one panel. Gas connection given as printed: listed 1/2" shut-off and flex connector to the 1/2" valve inlet, with a 3/8" x 18" connector supplied; the parts list also shows a 36" 3/8" gas line (into valve) and an 18" flex tube. The manual gives no efficiency, emissions or heating-area figures. The switch-only start on p. 60 (burner on HI from the rocker switch) has no heading in the text and isn't used. check_numbers: 0 unmatched numbers; part numbers verified verbatim separately.
